items.title: Avoiding finitely many prime ideals while staying in a fixed coset of an ideal
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma states that if the coset x + I is not contained in any of finitely many primes, then there is an element y of I with x + y outside all of them (statement lines 2813-2820). The proof does not use the general prime avoidance lemma in the form it is usually quoted: it removes inclusions among the primes, splits them by whether they contain x, finds an element of I outside the first bad prime together with a multiplier lying in all the earlier primes but not in that one, and adds their product to x, concluding by induction on the number of primes already avoided (proof lines 2822-2830). The construction of the adjusting element is the substance and the author writes out each step. H2.
